`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5,17` — `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is not null-checked (throws on pages that load the script before the div exists); `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison — compare against a normalized origin instead. Also no `sandbox` attribute on the injected iframe.
`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is copy-paste residue, unrelated to this job.
`app/models/topic_embed.rb:57` — `absolutize_urls` only handles `href`/`src` starting with `/`. Protocol-relative (`//cdn/...`) and document-relative (`images/x.png`) links are left broken.

`lib/topic_retriever.rb:44` — running `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline inside `RetrieveTopic` means one user hitting an unknown embed URL triggers a full feed parse; acceptable but worth a comment or a separate enqueue.

`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` — the `--category` option was removed with no replacement, silently changing behavior for existing users of the importer. Unrelated to the stated intent; call it out in the PR description or restore it.

`db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` — whitespace-only change that also removes the trailing newline; several new files also lack trailing newlines (`embed.css.scss`, `topic_retriever.rb`, both views).

No `topic_id`/`post_id` foreign keys or indexes on `topic_embeds`, and no `dependent:` handling — deleting a topic leaves an orphan row that makes `topic_id_for_embed` return a dead id, which will blow up `TopicView.new`.
No documentation/README for how a site owner actually installs `embed.js` (`discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals are undocumented outside the code).

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **3. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33` + `app/models/post.rb:131` — feed HTML is stored and rendered raw with no sanitization.**

adjudication.rationale: Real. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` the feed item HTML (`i.content`) is taken, minimally processed (`CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub` only), and passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw` set to that HTML. Then `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal rendering/cooking pipeline (where sanitization would typically occur). Finally, the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Net effect: arbitrary HTML from an external RSS/ATOM feed is stored and rendered as-is, enabling XSS if the feed contains unsafe markup.

The diff adds `force: true` to a new `create_table :topic_embeds` migration and changes an existing `create_table :top_topics` migration to include `force: true`. While `force: true` can be destructive if the table already exists (it drops/recreates), in the normal Rails migration flow these migrations run once on a fresh DB where the tables do not exist, so no verifiable bug/security/correctness issue is introduced by this diff alone. The change to an already-run migration also won’t affect existing installations because that migration would not be re-executed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **5. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33` — `i.content` assumed present; whole feed dies on the first item without it.**
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the code assumes `i.content` is always present, so an item lacking `content` can cause the feed processing to fail (consistent with a nil dereference risk). While it doesn’t explicitly mention `i.content.scrub` or the specific fallback to `description`, it identifies the same underlying nil-content crash issue.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `PostCreator.new(...).create` is called inside a transaction and the code checks `if post.present?` before creating the `TopicEmbed` record, then returns `post` at the end. There is no evidence in the diff that `PostCreator#create` “fails” in a way that is silently swallowed (exceptions would propagate; a non-created/invalid post would result in `nil`/non-present and be returned, which is a form of signaling). Also `skip_validations: true` reduces the likelihood of a validation-based failure. The finding asserts a defect without a verifiable failure mode shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **7. `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-20` — the "loading" response is cached for a minute and the retry loop is unbounded.**

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, after either rendering `loading` (when `topic_id` is nil) or `best`, it calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, which applies the same cache TTL to the loading response as well. The `loading.html.erb` view contains a `setTimeout` that calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no termination condition, so the retry loop is effectively unbounded. Because `location.reload()` may reuse cached content, the 1-minute caching can cause repeated reloads to keep serving the cached loading page rather than re-running the controller logic to detect when the topic is available, leading to excessive retries and potentially prolonged/indefinite “Loading” behavior.

`TopicEmbed.import` does append to the `contents` string in-place via `contents << ...`, which would mutate the caller’s string object. However, in the diff all shown call sites pass freshly-created strings (`CGI.unescapeHTML(...)` in `PollFeed`, `doc.content` in `import_remote`), and there’s no demonstrated reuse of the same string instance after calling `import`. So while the mutation is technically true, the finding does not identify a clear, verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by this diff—it's more of an API/purity/style concern unless a concrete reuse scenario exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **9. `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-48` — the test asserts an implementation the controller no longer has.**

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it never instantiates `TopicRetriever` or calls `retrieve`. However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the example around lines 44-48) expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called and `retriever.retrieve` to run. That expectation will fail against the controller code in this diff, so the test is asserting behavior the controller does not have.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **10. `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6` — `embed_url` is `string` (255 chars) with a unique index and no length validation.**

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as a Rails `string` (typically VARCHAR(255)) and adds a unique index on it, but the model only validates presence (`validates_presence_of :embed_url`) and the import path accepts any `http(s)` URL (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). URLs can exceed 255 characters; in that case saving may fail (DB error) or be truncated depending on DB/settings, and truncation combined with a unique index can cause false “duplicate” collisions. This is a concrete correctness risk introduced by the diff.

Also no `sandbox` attribute on the injected iframe.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags that `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` is only a substring check and not a proper origin comparison, recommending normalization/strict comparison. This is the same underlying bypass risk described in the golden comment (e.g., malicious domains passing via substring matching).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is copy-paste residue, unrelated to this job.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the first line `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is never referenced anywhere in that job (the job only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). This makes the require unnecessary and likely copy/paste residue, adding needless loading/coupling (and potential side effects) without benefit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:57` — `absolutize_urls` only handles `href`/`src` starting with `/`. Protocol-relative (`//cdn/...`) and document-relative (`images/x.png`) links are left broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the code only rewrites `a['href']`/`img['src']` when the value starts with `'/'` (`href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')`). Other common relative forms like protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) and document-relative paths (`images/x.png`, `../img.png`) are not rewritten, so they will remain as-is in the imported HTML and can break when rendered in Discourse. This is directly verifiable from the method implementation and its stated intent (“Convert any relative URLs to absolute”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:44` — running `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline inside `RetrieveTopic` means one user hitting an unknown embed URL triggers a full feed parse; acceptable but worth a comment or a separate enqueue.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb). TopicRetriever is invoked from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job that is enqueued by EmbedController when an embed URL has no existing TopicEmbed. This means a single embed request for an unknown URL can trigger a full feed fetch/parse immediately in the worker, potentially repeatedly for many distinct embed URLs (the 60s throttle is per-embed_url key, not a global feed throttle). This is a real performance/abuse-risk concern introduced by the diff (doing heavy scheduled work inline/on-demand) rather than just a style nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` — the `--category` option was removed with no replacement, silently changing behavior for existing users of the importer. Unrelated to the stated intent; call it out in the PR description or restore it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category` and also deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it to `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The importer now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` with no category handling, so existing users/scripts relying on `--category` will lose that functionality with no in-code replacement. This is a concrete, verifiable behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` — whitespace-only change that also removes the trailing newline; several new files also lack trailing newlines (`embed.css.scss`, `topic_retriever.rb`, both views).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show files with `\ No newline at end of file` (e.g., `embed.css.scss`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, and `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`). However, missing trailing newlines and whitespace-only changes are formatting/style issues, not a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the change, and the migration’s behavior is unchanged. Under the stated criteria, this is not a “real problem.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: No `topic_id`/`post_id` foreign keys or indexes on `topic_embeds`, and no `dependent:` handling — deleting a topic leaves an orphan row that makes `topic_id_for_embed` return a dead id, which will blow up `TopicView.new`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` columns but only adds a unique index on `embed_url` and does not add foreign keys. The `TopicEmbed` model has `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no `dependent:` cleanup on the owning models (and no FK constraints). `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and, if it returns an id, immediately does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` rather than verifying the topic exists. If a topic/post is deleted later, the `topic_embeds` row can become orphaned; `topic_id_for_embed` would still return the stale id and `TopicView.new` is likely to raise (or at least behave incorrectly) instead of enqueuing retrieval. This is a real correctness issue introduced/left unhandled by the diff (the indexing point is more perf-oriented, but the orphan/stale-id behavior is verifiable from the new code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No documentation/README for how a site owner actually installs `embed.js` (`discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals are undocumented outside the code).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new embedding assets (embed.js/embed.css) and an embed endpoint, but it does not touch any documentation files. While it's true that this diff itself doesn't add a README explaining how to include embed.js or define `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl`, that is not a verifiable defect introduced by the code change: documentation may already exist elsewhere outside the diff, and the lack of new docs is not a correctness/bug/security issue that can be confirmed from the patch alone.
